newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rebel leader gets kidney transplant.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rebel leader gets kidney transplant.

text.p: A Mexican rebel leader said only six weeks ago to be on the verge of death was recovering in a Mexico City private hospital on Wednesday after a kidney transplant, doctors said.
Zapatista rebel leader Commander Ramona, a Tzotzil Maya Indian woman, received the kidney on Sunday after one of her brothers donated the organ, they said.
"The state of health of the patient, though delicate, is good," surgeon Arturo Dib Cury, one of the doctors who carried out the operation, told reporters.
Ramona travelled from a rebel base in the Lacandon Jungle in the southeastern state of Chiapas to Mexico City six weeks ago after the government of President Ernesto Zedillo gave her safe conduct.

It was a conciliatory gesture by the Zedillo administration towards the Zapatista rebels. The government openly says it prefers dealing with the Chiapas rebels to more radical leftist rebel groups that have appeared in other parts of Mexico this year.

Ramona, about 40 and barely four feet (1.22 metres) tall, won the hearts of many Mexicans when she first appeared in public, masked and dwarfed by her fellow Zapatista commanders, at a first round of peace talks with the government in February 1994, in the colonial city of San Cristobal de las Casas.

The Zapatistas rose up in arms on New Year's Day 1994 to demand indigenous rights and greater democracy. About 145 people died in the early days of the rebellion but there has been little fighting since.

Often rumoured to have died in subsequent months, she struck a propaganda blow for the rebels last month by attending an indigenous meeting in Mexico City and addressing Zapatista supporters there before entering hospital.
Zapatista military leader and spokesman Subcommander Marcos said then that travelling to the capital was "her last wish before dying" and that she had a "terminal illness."
The exact nature of her kidney complaint was not clear but she had widely been reported to be suffering from cancer.
